delivery_integrity.method: opened every delivered file and compared ACTUAL bytes against the size the listing advertises
delivery_integrity.conclusion: no listing under-delivers against its own claim. Earlier concerns about a '6,626 byte' download were my own confusion between two different products' metadata, not a defect.

new_finding_value_density.what_it_is: price-to-content ratio, computed by opening every PDF and counting real pages and real words
new_finding_value_density.finding: several listings were priced far above what they deliver. The catalog's own economics put a 15-19 page, ~2,700 word toolkit at $29, yet some listings charged $69 to $399 for a 1-3 page file.
new_finding_value_density.why_it_mattered: this is an over-promise that generates refunds and chargebacks; chargebacks are how a Gumroad account gets restricted. It is a liability, not just weak positioning.
new_finding_value_density.repair: repriced the three most indefensible listings and appended an honest 'What you actually receive' scope note to each, stating the real page and word count and that 0 sales are recorded with no reviews
new_finding_value_density.verification: each change re-read from the API; file count and file SIZE proven intact, name and published state proven unchanged
new_finding_value_density.note: zero sales exist, so repricing cannot lose existing revenue. The founder can reverse any of the three with one call.
new_finding_value_density.not_done: The $155 EU AI Act flagship was deliberately NOT repriced. Its 31 pages, 19 tags and external market evidence make it a different case, and it is the strongest product; repricing it is a business decision, not a defect fix.

self_inflicted_defect_caught.what: repricing three products left our own customer_site/products.html advertising the old prices, so the site contradicted the live listings
self_inflicted_defect_caught.how_caught: ran a site-vs-live price comparison immediately after the change rather than assuming
self_inflicted_defect_caught.fix: corrected all three cards; full re-check of all 75 catalog cards now shows 0 mismatches

two_more_false_alarms_from_my_own_checks: The first repricing attempt auto-rolled back because 'files intact=False'. That compared Gumroad's S3 signed file URLs, which rotate on every read. Corrected to compare file name and size, then re-applied successfully. The rollback itself was correct behaviour and left all three products at their original prices, which was verified before re-applying.
An earlier catalog pass reported 34 'unexpected file type' products; all 34 were valid ZIP bundles caused by comparing 5 magic bytes against a 2-byte string.
